users.removeConfirmDesc: This will permanently delete {username} and all of their data. They will lose access immediately.
users.tokensDesc: Metadata only — token names are never shown here, because they are free text the user wrote and can be revealing on their own. You can revoke a token, but never issue one on someone's behalf. Every revocation is recorded in the audit log and sent to the user's inbox.
users.tokensEmpty: This user has no access tokens.
users.tokenRevokeConfirmDesc: The token stops working immediately and the user is told in their inbox. This cannot be undone.
users.emailTitle: Set or clear the email address
users.emailDesc: Use this when the address on the account can't be reached — a dead mailbox, a lapsed domain, or an address taken along with the account. Users change their own address from their profile, which needs approval from both addresses.
users.emailWarning: The address is saved as verified, with no confirmation email. Saving also signs the user out of every device and revokes all their access tokens, and cancels any change they had in progress.

invitations.revokeConfirmDesc: This invitation link will no longer work.
invitations.notePlaceholder: e.g. John Smith, expires after camp

settings.llmDesc: Configure the LLM presets used across this instance. The first preset is the default.
settings.modelDefaultHint: Default model, used when a user hasn't picked one. Add it to the selectable models below to attach body params.
settings.apiKeySet: Key configured — enter a new value to replace it
settings.testNoBaseUrl: Add a preset first before testing
settings.extraHeadersDesc: Added to every outbound LLM request — e.g. a provider's zero-data-retention header.
settings.modelsDesc: The presets users can choose from — e.g. Anthropic, Mistral. The first preset is the instance default. Each carries its own base URL, model, key, headers and body params. Body values are read as JSON where possible.
settings.structuredOutputsDesc: Send a strict JSON schema so plan/workout generation conforms exactly. Leave on unless this provider rejects it.
settings.analysisContextDesc: Optional coaching context injected into every activity analysis for this instance. Describe the sport, training philosophy, or any standing instructions for the AI coach.
settings.analysisContextPlaceholder: e.g. This is an elite road cycling team. Prioritise power-based metrics and threshold training. Responses should be concise and data-driven.
settings.adminContactDesc: Shown to users on the password-reset screen. Leave blank to hide it.
settings.allowSelfSignupDesc: When on, anyone can register with their email address and verify it. Requires a configured email provider; invitations always work regardless.
settings.requiresSubscriptionDesc: When on, only users with AI access (or their own AI model via BYOK) can use this instance’s AI features.
settings.requiresSubscriptionWarning: Users without AI access or their own AI model will be blocked from AI features until you grant them access.
settings.allowTokensDesc: Let users issue long-lived, scoped credentials to their own tooling — backup scripts, cron jobs, phones, external AI clients. A token grants strictly less than the session its owner already holds: it is scoped, and never reaches the admin API, /api/auth, the inbox or AI features.
settings.allowTokensWarning: Turning this off refuses authentication, not just issuance: tokens issued earlier stop working immediately.
settings.allowMcpDesc: Publish the Model Context Protocol endpoint (POST /mcp), where an AI client — Claude Desktop, an IDE, a CLI — can call read-only coaching tools over the training data of whoever's credential it holds. Every tool declares the read scopes it needs, so a token reaches exactly what it was granted and nothing else.
settings.allowMcpWarning: The endpoint is refused outright, the handshake included, so a client is told the server is not there rather than connecting and then failing every call. This withdraws an interface, not an exposure: a token reaches the same data through the ordinary API either way — what limits a credential is its scopes.
settings.allowMcpNeedsTokens: Personal access tokens are off, so no external client has a credential to connect with. The endpoint is published but unreachable in practice.
settings.allowCourseReconDesc: Upload a GPX course and get a segment table and a written pacing plan. Off by default, because classifying the road surface under a course needs a routing sidecar you run and build map tiles for yourself.
settings.allowCourseReconWarning: Off withdraws the whole feature — courses, the segment table, the pacing plan and bikes all become unavailable. Nothing is deleted: stored courses stay exactly where they are, remain in every data export, and come back untouched when you turn this on.
settings.allowCourseReconSidecar: Road surfaces are a separate, optional step: without a routing sidecar configured, every course is solved as dry pavement — which the written plan says out loud.

usage.desc: Token usage for instance-paid AI calls. Calls made through users’ own AI models (BYOK) are not counted.
